title: tenant telemetry recovery and dashboard widget restore
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: Multiple enterprise customers reported missing metrics and ‘no data’ widgets across the Console during a high-load window on 2026-03-09. Secondary symptom: trace spans were not linking to ingestion events for a subset of Tenant IDs, causing broken trace->metric navigation and stale live panels. Scope: Hosted + Dedicated control plane routing and backbone aggregator; Private instances with older ingestion agents were affected by a schema mismatch. Goals: stabilize ingestion for affected tenants, restore dashboard widgets, replay/backfill missing metrics, and patch the root cause to prevent recurrence.
impact_timeline: 2026-03-09 02:12 UTC - First SE ticket (Acct: NovaHealth) reports missing QPS metric on /api/requests for their production workspace.
2026-03-09 02:35 UTC - Additional reports from two Dedicated customers; on-call paged; Incident declared.
2026-03-09 03:05 UTC - Initial mitigations: increase ingestion router replicas and enable higher trace sampling for affected partitions.
2026-03-09 05:40 UTC - Hotfix (ingest-router v1.14.3) rolled to canary; metrics reappeared for 60% of affected tenants.
2026-03-09 07:20 UTC - Hotfix promoted to production; full restore by 2026-03-09 08:10 UTC for hosted and Dedicated control plane.
2026-03-09 11:00 UTC - Follow-up CVE/agent upgrade required for Private customers using agent v0.9.1; customer patch window scheduled.
root_cause_analysis: Primary cause: a rolling change to the upstream telemetry schema (field 'tenant_v2') was deployed to the ingest-router without backward-compatibility for legacy agent payloads. During high concurrency, the router's fast-path validation dropped payloads with unexpected schema versions rather than queuing them for transformation.

Secondary cause: trace->metric stitching used a best-effort tenant-id mapping that relied on a recently-introduced cache eviction heuristic; eviction was aggressive under load and caused missed joins between spans and metrics for specific tenant sharding keys.

Why it escaped testing: integration tests used uniform tenant identifiers and did not exercise interleaved legacy/modern agent payload mixes; performance testing did not simulate the schema mismatch pattern.
decisions_and_tradeoffs: Ship a two-part fix: (A) immediate safe-backwards-compatible ingest-router behavior that accepts legacy payloads and drops only non-critical unknown fields; (B) longer-term: introduce partition-aware schema transformation pipeline with an opportunistic backfill capability.
Tradeoff: the immediate fix increases CPU on ingest-router by ~4% (measured in canary) but avoids customer-visible data loss. We accepted the small cost increase to protect production SLAs.
For Private customers we will not auto-upgrade agents; instead we provide a migration guide and a one-click patch for customers who opt-in during maintenance windows.
implementation_notes: ingest-router: add permissive-schema flag and fallback transformer (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest-router/pull/624).
kvcache-stitcher: adjust eviction thresholds and add tenant-affinity sticky buckets (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/kvcache-stitcher/pull/219).
replayer service: small tool to replay archived raw batches (S3 path prefixes) into the new pipeline for backfill (Repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/replayer, PR #18).
Canary rollout: 10% -> 50% -> 100% with 15-minute observation windows and SLO checks using Console live metrics dashboard 'ingest.health.overall'.
qa_steps: End-to-end: send mixed legacy and modern payloads for tenant set A; assert that time-series for 5 key metrics appear within 60s.
Trace linking: produce a synthetic trace span and corresponding metric event; verify console trace->metric link resolves and opens span details.
Load regression: run k6 script (scripts/ingest_schema_stress.js) at 1.5x typical peak and validate 99th percentile ingest latency does not regress >20%.
Private validation: provide a Docker image with patched agent and run compatibility shim against on-prem telemetry collector; checklist in Confluence.
rollback_plan: If consumer error rates increase >5% or new 'schema_error' logs spike: toggle permissive-schema=false via runtime flag and roll back ingest-router to v1.14.2.
Rollback will be done per-region, starting with non-US regions to limit blast radius; communication via #incident-ops and customer-facing status pages.
deploy_and_monitoring: Deployed ingest-router v1.14.3-canary on 2026-03-09 05:40 UTC; production promotion 07:20 UTC.
Monitors created: 'ingest.router.schema_errors', 'kvcache.stitch_miss_rate', 'dash.widget.no_data_rate'. Alerts: page on >1% sustained schema_errors for 5m.
Post-deploy: sampling confirmed restored metrics for 98% of affected tenants; ongoing small cohort (2%) needed manual replay due to archival expiration window.
customer_communications: SE thread: initial acknowledgement to customers at 2026-03-09 02:48 UTC; status updates at 03:30, 06:00, 09:15 UTC.
Status page: incident entry 'INC-2026-031' created and updated until resolved. Link: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2026-031
Customer follow-up: offered a data-replay for time windows where metrics were missing and a 10% billing credit as good will for the impacted window.
review_feedback: PM (Isabel Romero) - approved immediate hotfix but requested retention policy review for archived batches used by replayer.
Security (Jonas Krüger) - confirmed permissive-schema flag does not introduce injection vectors; recommended additional input sanitization in transformer.
Design (Priya Shah) - asked for clearer Console widget state for partial data (new UI state 'partial' vs 'no data') to avoid customer confusion.

ENG-68421 - improve archival retention metrics and alerting for replayer eligibility
PM-402 - ship Console UX update to show 'partial data' state and tooltip guidance

acceptance_criteria: All affected tenant dashboards show consistent time-series for the impacted window after replay/backfill or are marked 'partial' with clear messaging
Trace->metric linking resolves for synthetic end-to-end tests in staging and production canary
No increase in schema_error rate after 48h post-deploy and CPU increase remains within expected range
